OpenGLRenderer::UpdateSceneLighting stores m_currentLighting and sets on the lit program: uEncodeOutput = (colorSpace == Linear && (!m_framebufferIsSrgb || forceShaderEncode)), uAmbientLight, uCameraPos, uNumDirectionalLights = min(size, MAX_DIRECTIONAL_LIGHTS) and uDirectionalLights[i].{direction,color,intensity}, the same for point lights (position, color, intensity, range, attenuation; MAX 8) and spot lights (position, direction, color, intensity, range, cosInner/cosOuter computed on the CPU from innerConeAngle/outerConeAngle; MAX 4): read the exact code (including how an inner angle at or past the outer one is handled) and mirror it byte for byte into the 752-byte std140 block. renderer/include/renderer/common/SceneLighting.hpp: ColorSpace {Gamma, Linear}, SceneLightingData {ambientColor (default 0.2), colorSpace (Gamma), forceShaderEncode, the three vectors, MAX_* = 2/8/4}. GL renders into SRGB8_ALPHA8 and toggles GL_FRAMEBUFFER_SRGB per draw only for the lit shader in linear lighting; Vulkan's target is R8G8B8A8_UNORM, so on Vulkan uEncodeOutput = (colorSpace == Linear) ? 1 : 0 and forceShaderEncode changes nothing (document it); unlit (and later text) are identical in both colour spaces. sRGB textures (stage A: VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB for 3/4-channel options.srgb, UNORM fallback with a log when the device cannot sample it) decode on sampling in BOTH colour spaces, as GL's SRGB8_ALPHA8 does (the software renderer decodes in both too, but AFTER filtering, GL/Vulkan BEFORE: expect small differences for linear-filtered sRGB textures, which is what the lit tolerance is for). The software renderer: renderer/src/software/SoftwareRenderer.cpp (UpdateSceneLighting stores m_lighting/m_cameraPos; lit/PBR shading, emissive after lighting, occlusion scales ambient only, normal map handedness, LinearToSrgb). SCOPE: (1) Lit shader DRAWS: GetStandardLitShader returns the lit built-in when HasBuiltInShaders() (else nullptr with the existing once-only reason); IsValidShader true for it; DestroyShaderProgram of it refused. GetStandardTextShader stays the IRenderer default nullptr (stage E). (2) VulkanMaterial for the lit shader: CreateMaterial(litShader[, texture]) returns a registered material with EXACTLY the GL lit defaults listed above, all written through the name table (the block is the shader's std140 layout from VulkanShaderInterface.hpp; kMaterialBlockRange 128 stays the descriptor range); Set*/SetColor/SetTexture/SetAuxTexture/GetAuxTexture as in stage B; materials of the text shader or foreign/null shaders still return nullptr (stage E); the snapshot at DrawMesh covers the lit block and all five textures. (3) Aux textures with defaults: the five samplers (base, Emissive, Occlusion, Normal, MetallicRoughness in AuxTexture order) bind the material's textures, an absent or destroyed one the renderer-owned 1x1 default (stage B's values: keep them unless a golden proves GL differs, then say so in `deviations`); the uHas*Texture flags are what Material::ApplyUniforms sets (the renderer does not infer them), matching GL and the software renderer's 'an invalid texture is stored as none so the flags agree with what is drawn' behaviour where the renderer is responsible for it (read SoftwareEmissiveTest.AnInvalidTextureIsStoredAsNoneSoTheHasTextureFlagsAgreeWithWhatIsDrawn and decide; document). Normal-map handedness (tangent.w), mirrored model matrices and a mesh without tangents behave as GL (the lit.frag port already does the maths; prove it with the tests below). (4) UpdateSceneLighting UBO: fill the 752-byte std140 Lighting block (uCameraPos, uEncodeOutput, uAmbientLight, the counts clamped to 2/8/4, the light arrays with the exact std140 struct layouts the lit.frag declares, spot cosInner/cosOuter computed as GL does). It is called INSIDE the frame (after BeginFrame), possibly more than once per frame, and stage B has ONE lighting buffer bound by every frame slot: writing it while the other slot's frame may still read it is a race the validation layer will not always catch. Required semantics = GL's: a draw uses the lighting set by the last UpdateSceneLighting BEFORE that draw (an UpdateSceneLighting after a draw does not change it; the next frame's update does not change the previous frame in flight). Recommended: keep a CPU copy of the block, and at the first lit draw after each UpdateSceneLighting (per frame) copy it into the current frame's ring and bind it with a dynamic offset (frame set binding 1 becomes UNIFORM_BUFFER_DYNAMIC, so the frame set gets two dynamic offsets; keep layouts shared), or use one lighting buffer per frame slot written only after that slot's fence wait plus a ring copy on a second update in the same frame; choose, document the choice in VulkanDraw.cpp, and delete/retire the stage B single buffer correctly (Shutdown frees everything before VMA and the device; internalAllocations stays accurate). UpdateSceneLighting outside BeginFrame..EndFrame just stores the values (used by the next frame's draws). Before the first UpdateSceneLighting of the renderer's life a lit draw uses a defined default (SceneLightingData{} with the camera at the origin, as the software renderer's members default to; check and match it). (5) Linear encode / sRGB handling: as above (UNORM target, uEncodeOutput = Linear, sRGB textures decode on sampling, data maps UNORM). Do NOT add an sRGB render target. (6) The parity test (VulkanShaderParityTests.cpp, device-free) is EXTENDED: the lighting block is now checked member by member, including the light structs' members, their std140 offsets inside the struct and the array strides (the std140 calculator gains struct and array support), against the GLSL; every name OpenGLRenderer::UpdateSceneLighting sets (uEncodeOutput, uAmbientLight, uCameraPos, uNum*Lights, and the struct member names it builds as 'uDirectionalLights[i].direction' etc.) has a matching lighting-table/struct entry; every default OpenGLRenderer::CreateMaterial sets for the LIT shader has a table entry of the right type; the C++ code that fills the lighting block uses the table offsets (no second hard-coded copy of the offsets, or a static_assert tying them). Keep the threading model (one renderer mutex; VulkanMaterial's own mutex); IRenderer unchanged.

HARNESS FIX FIRST (REVIEW LOW carried from stage B, MUST be done BEFORE any lit scene relies on the diff): CrossBackendDiff.hpp's 'share' mode (maxFractionOverSecond > 0) is looser than the proposal's lit rule: it has NO mean-error criterion, and pixels whose difference lies between `tolerance` and `secondThreshold` can never fail it. Add the proposal's lit criterion explicitly (e.g. a mode or Options fields such as maxMeanError = 2.0/255-units and a per-pixel mean over the compared pixels' channel differences, documented whether the mean is over the max channel or over all RGB channels; pick the stricter reading unless the observed numbers force otherwise and then list it in `deviations`): a lit comparison passes only when the MEAN error over the compared pixels is <= 2/255 AND at most 1% of the compared pixels exceed 8/255, so in-between pixels count through the mean; report the mean in Result::Describe. Also fix the coverage-edge exclusion for lit scenes: CoverageEdges today marks every pixel whose RGB differs from ANY neighbour, which in a smoothly shaded lit scene marks almost every covered pixel and would silently exclude the whole image. Base the exclusion on COVERAGE (e.g. a per-pixel coverage/ID mask rendered with flat unlit colours for the same geometry on both backends, or a neighbour difference over a large threshold), keep the proposal's 1-pixel border, and FAIL the comparison when the excluded share exceeds a documented cap (e.g. more than 25% of the image, or of the covered pixels) so an over-broad exclusion can never pass vacuously. Keep the strict unlit mode's behaviour and the stage B unlit goldens passing unchanged (if the edge definition changes, the strict unlit callers must still pass with the same or a narrower exclusion; say so). Add device-free tests of the harness itself (e.g. tests/renderer/vulkan/CrossBackendDiffTests.cpp, plain TESTs, run on every Vulkan-ON leg): an image pair where EVERY pixel differs by 7/255 must FAIL the lit criterion (mean 7 > 2, although no pixel is over 8); every pixel off by 1-2/255 passes; 0.5% of pixels off by 50/255 with the rest exact passes, 2% off by 50/255 fails; a strict-mode pair with one pixel off by 3/255 fails; a smooth gradient scene is NOT wholly excluded as 'edges' (the excluded share is small) and the exclusion cap trips when it is exceeded; size mismatch and 'nothing compared' fail.
